answer: Require every agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can trade, and let that stake be slashed if peers catch it misbehaving. A newcomer starts on the terrace of the market with limited volume, earning wider access only through a history of honest deals, like a sonnet whose every stanza must scan before the next is trusted. A raven watchtower of random peer audits samples transactions, so spinning up a thousand fake identities multiplies the stake cost and the chance of detection instead of multiplying profit.
